finding.claim: /preview fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side with no scheme, host, or IP validation, and returns the response body to the caller, so it is a full-read SSRF.

trace.note: requests.get(target) — no validation, redirects followed by default
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] returned in JSON, giving the attacker a read channel

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No allowlist, no scheme check, no private/loopback/link-local IP block, no allow_redirects=False, no DNS pinning. Only the 5s timeout and 500-char truncation apply, and neither limits the target. Case 04/12 patterns apply; no decoy matches.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 reads the attacker-controlled `url` query parameter, app.py:16 passes it unvalidated to requests.get (redirects followed by default), and app.py:17 returns the status and first 500 chars of the body, so /preview is a full-read SSRF; the host allowlist at app.py:24 exists only on the separate /partner route (lines 20-27) and does not cover /preview.

finding.claim: /partner checks the hostname of the initial URL against an allowlist, but requests.get follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted host can redirect the server to an internal or non-allowlisted address (for example http://169.254.169.254/ or http://127.0.0.1/), bypassing the check.
finding.sink: app.py:26 requests.get(target, timeout=5) with redirects enabled

trace.note: host = urlparse(target).hostname — parsed only for the check
host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS → 400; passes only for api.partner.example or cdn.partner.example
requests.get(target) re-sends the raw string and follows 3xx Location headers without re-checking the host

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist on the initial URL (app.py:23-25): case-insensitive and exact-match, so suffix tricks like evil.partner.example fail. Scheme is effectively limited to http/https by requests. Not checked: redirect targets (allow_redirects not disabled), resolved IP (private/loopback/metadata ranges), and port. Exploitation requires an allowlisted partner host that returns a redirect, or an open redirect on one of them. Severity is lower than SSRF-1. Also, urlparse and urllib3 may disagree on certain malformed authorities (for example backslash-based forms); I did not verify this, so it is not reported as a separate finding.

verdict.guard_found: Only the exact-match hostname check at app.py:23-24 (ALLOWED_HOSTS membership on urlparse(target).hostname). It runs once on the initial URL and does not cover redirect targets. requests.get at app.py:26 uses default allow_redirects for GET, and nothing after it re-validates the destination. No IP or private-range check and no redirect disabling exists anywhere in app.py.
verdict.reason: The source is the unauthenticated `url` query parameter (app.py:22), and the only closing check is the initial exact-host allowlist at app.py:23-24; requests.get at app.py:26 follows 3xx redirects to any host with no re-check, so the bypass is real. Exploitation is conditional: it needs an allowlisted partner host that issues a redirect or an open redirect on one, which is outside this code, so severity should stay below SSRF-1.
